questions.question:
What actions did Vijayalaya Chola take after capturing the Kaveri delta?

I. He established the town of Thanjavur.

II. He built a temple for the goddess Nishumbhasudini.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayalaya Chola** captured the **Kaveri delta**, marking the beginning of the Chola dynasty's resurgence in South India. This region was strategically important due to its fertile lands and proximity to trade routes.
 
• After capturing the Kaveri delta, Vijayalaya Chola established the **town of Thanjavur**, which later became the capital and a cultural hub for the Cholas. *This statement is correct.*
 
• Vijayalaya Chola also built a **temple for the goddess Nishumbhasudini** (a form of Durga) in Thanjavur to commemorate his victory and to signify the divine approval of his rule. This temple was an important religious and cultural landmark. *This statement is correct.*
 
• Both actions—establishing Thanjavur and constructing the temple—reflect Vijayalaya Chola’s efforts to consolidate political authority and establish religious and cultural legitimacy.
 
• These developments laid the foundation for the Chola dynasty's future prosperity and dominance in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vijayalaya Chola:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Imperial Chola dynasty** in the 9th century CE.
 
• He emerged as a powerful ruler after defeating the Pallavas and Pandya rulers in the Kaveri delta region.
 
• His reign marked the rise of the Cholas as a dominant power in South India after centuries of decline.
 
 
 
• **Thanjavur:**
 
 
• Thanjavur became the **political and cultural capital** of the Chola dynasty during its peak.
 
• The city was known for its architectural marvels, including the **Brihadeeswarar Temple**, built later by Rajaraja Chola I.
 
• It served as a center for art, literature, and religion under Chola patronage.
 
 
 
• **Temple of Goddess Nishumbhasudini:**
 
 
• Vijayalaya Chola built this temple to honor the goddess and to signify his victory over enemies.
 
• The temple reflects the importance of **religion and divine authority** in legitimizing kingship during ancient times.
 
• The goddess Nishumbhasudini represents the **triumph of good over evil**, symbolizing Vijayalaya’s own victory.
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its contributions to **art, architecture, administration, and maritime trade**.
 
• It reached its zenith under rulers like **Rajaraja Chola I** and **Rajaraja Chola II**.
 
• The Cholas were also known for their naval prowess, which helped them establish trade routes and cultural ties with Southeast Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Chola dynasty's resurgence under Vijayalaya Chola marked the beginning of a significant era in South Indian history. It was characterized by advancements in architecture, literature, and governance.
 
• Thanjavur, established by Vijayalaya, became a model city that symbolized the grandeur of the Chola empire.
 
• Religious patronage, such as building temples, was a common practice among rulers to demonstrate their piety and gain public support.
 
• The Cholas’ emphasis on temple construction and patronage of the arts played a pivotal role in the cultural development of South India.

questions.question: Which Rajputs refused to accept the authority of the Mughals for a long time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sisodiya Rajputs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Sisodiya Rajputs**, primarily ruling from **Mewar**, were known for their fierce independence and refusal to accept the authority of the Mughals for a long time.

• The most notable Sisodiya ruler, **Maharana Pratap**, resisted Mughal emperor Akbar's attempts to annex Mewar and fought the famous **Battle of Haldighati** in **1576**.

• Even after their defeat in Haldighati, the Sisodiyas continued guerrilla warfare under Maharana Pratap and later rulers, maintaining their sovereignty over parts of Mewar.

• Unlike other Rajput clans such as the **Kachhwaha** of Amer and the **Rathores** of Marwar, who allied with the Mughals and served in their administration, the Sisodiyas upheld their policy of defiance.

• The Sisodiya Rajputs are celebrated in Indian history for their valor, dedication to their homeland, and their commitment to maintaining independence, making them a symbol of resistance against Mughal imperialism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Maharana Pratap:**

• Maharana Pratap (1540–1597) was the most famous ruler of the Sisodiya dynasty and is remembered for his valiant resistance against the Mughal empire.

• He refused to accept Mughal suzerainty, unlike most other Rajput rulers, and chose to fight rather than surrender.

• He established his capital at **Chavand** after losing Chittorgarh to the Mughals.

• Even after the Battle of Haldighati, he continued a guerrilla war against Akbar and reclaimed much of his lost territory.

• **Battle of Haldighati (1576):**

• The battle was fought between Maharana Pratap and the Mughal forces led by **Man Singh I of Amber**, a Rajput who had allied with Akbar.

• Though inconclusive, the battle demonstrated the fierce resistance of Maharana Pratap and his determination to defend his kingdom.

• Pratap's loyal horse, **Chetak**, is also remembered for its bravery during this battle.

• **Other Rajput Clans:**

• The **Kachhwaha Rajputs** of Amer, under Raja Bharmal and later Raja Man Singh, allied with Akbar and became prominent commanders in his army.

• The **Rathore Rajputs** of Marwar also formed alliances with the Mughals, with rulers like Rao Maldeo and Jaswant Singh serving in the Mughal court.

• The **Chauhans** were significant during earlier medieval times but had lesser political influence during the Mughal period.

• **Rajput Resistance:**

• While many Rajput clans collaborated with the Mughals, the Sisodiyas' resistance became a defining feature of their legacy.

• This resistance inspired future leaders and symbolized the Rajput spirit of independence and valor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Chittorgarh:** The historic capital of the Sisodiya Rajputs and a significant symbol of Rajput pride. It was besieged multiple times by Muslim rulers, including Alauddin Khilji and Akbar.

• **Akbar's Rajput Policy:** Akbar adopted a strategy of alliance and diplomacy with Rajput rulers, offering them positions in his administration and matrimonial alliances to secure their loyalty.

• **Guerrilla Warfare:** Maharana Pratap effectively used guerrilla tactics against the Mughal forces, exploiting the rugged terrain of Mewar to his advantage.

• **Rajput Heritage:** The Sisodiya Rajputs' legacy of resistance is celebrated in Indian folklore, literature, and art, with Maharana Pratap becoming a national hero.

questions.question: 'Al Kiran' in India is a pioneering initiative co-led by the _________

options.text: Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
National Association of Software and Service Companies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **'Al Kiran'** is a pioneering initiative in India co-led by the **Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA)** to the Government of India.

• The **Principal Scientific Adviser** plays a key role in advising on science and technology policies and their application for national development.

• The initiative focuses on fostering innovation, enabling the application of scientific research, and promoting sustainable development in India.

• It aims to address critical challenges in areas such as healthcare, agriculture, energy, and education through the use of science and technology.

• The **Office of the PSA** collaborates with various stakeholders, including research institutions, industry leaders, and government agencies, to implement such initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA):**

• The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser was established in **1999** by the Government of India.

• The PSA's role includes providing **science and technology advice** to the Prime Minister and the Cabinet for formulating policies and strategies.

• It works to promote synergy between academia, industry, and government for scientific and technological advancements.

• The office also oversees the implementation of national missions and initiatives like **National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)** and other innovation-driven programs.

• **Key Functions of the PSA Office:**

• Advising on **strategic science and technology policies**.

• Collaborating with international organizations to promote global partnerships in science and technology.

• Overseeing the implementation of major national projects, such as those aimed at solving **climate change, energy security, and public health challenges**.

• **Other Relevant Organizations:**

• **NITI Aayog:** Focuses on policy formulation and economic development but is not directly involved in the 'Al Kiran' initiative.

• **Confederation of Indian Industry (CII):** Primarily represents industrial bodies and works on economic growth initiatives.

• **National Association of Software and Service Companies (NASSCOM):** Represents the IT and software services industry in India.

• **Importance of 'Al Kiran':**

• The initiative reflects India's commitment to leveraging **science and technology** for sustainable development.

• It emphasizes the need for innovation-driven solutions to address critical societal challenges.

• 'Al Kiran' serves as a model for integrating scientific research with policy-making and implementation at the national level.

</ul

questions.question: What is the minimum annual contribution (in Rs.) required to open and maintain an NPS Vatsalya account launched in September 20247
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **NPS Vatsalya account**, introduced in **September 2024**, is a new initiative under the National Pension Scheme (NPS) aimed at providing financial security.

• The minimum annual contribution required to open and maintain this account is **Rs. 1000**, making it accessible for a broad segment of the population.

• This initiative is particularly tailored to encourage savings for retirement and financial protection for individuals.

• The NPS Vatsalya account follows the broader framework of the NPS, emphasizing tax benefits and flexible investment options.

• Contributors can build a retirement corpus over time with relatively low annual contributions, ensuring inclusivity and financial planning for individuals across different income groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **About NPS:**

• The **National Pension Scheme (NPS)** is a government-sponsored pension scheme launched in **2004** for government employees and extended to all citizens in **2009**.

• It aims to provide financial security in old age through regular contributions over an individual’s working life.

• Investors can choose between various asset classes, such as equities, corporate bonds, and government securities, for their contributions.

• Subscribers receive a regular pension after retirement, based on the corpus accumulated during their working years.

• **Features of NPS Vatsalya:**

• The **NPS Vatsalya account** has been introduced to expand the reach of the NPS scheme and encourage savings among lower-income groups.

• It requires a **minimum annual contribution of Rs. 1000**, which is affordable for most individuals.

• The scheme offers **tax benefits** under Section 80C and Section 80CCD of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

• Flexibility in contributions allows subscribers to save and grow their retirement corpus according to their financial capacity.

• **Benefits of the NPS:**

• Subscribers receive a **fixed monthly pension** after retirement, depending on the accumulated savings.

• Investments under NPS are managed by professional fund managers, ensuring optimal returns for subscribers.

• Partial withdrawals are permitted under specific conditions, such as education, marriage, or critical illness.

• **Eligibility for NPS Vatsalya Account:**

• Any Indian citizen between the **ages of 18 and 65** can open an NPS Vatsalya account.

• The scheme is designed to promote financial inclusion among individuals in both urban and rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Comparison of Contribution Limits:**

• The **minimum annual contribution** for an NPS Vatsalya account is **Rs. 1000**, which is lower than the typical minimum contribution required for regular NPS accounts.

• There is **no upper limit** for contributions, allowing individuals to save more based on their financial goals.

• **Tax Benefits:**

• Contributions to the NPS are eligible for tax deductions of up to **Rs. 1.5 lakh** under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act.

• Additional deductions of up to **Rs. 50,000** are available under Section 80CCD(1B), making it an attractive savings tool.

• **Withdrawal Rules:**

• Subscribers can withdraw up to **25%** of their contributions after completing three years in the scheme, for specific purposes such as higher education or medical emergencies.

• At retirement, subscribers must use at least **40%** of their corpus to purchase an annuity, ensuring a steady income post-retirement.

• **Role of PFRDA:**

• The **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** regulates the NPS and ensures its smooth functioning.

• The PFRDA also approves and monitors fund managers responsible for managing subscribers’ investments.

questions.question:
Which of the following is one of the parameters of Financial Inclusion Index in India?

1. Access

II. Usage
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** was introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **July 2021**. It measures the level of financial inclusion in the country.

• The index comprises three parameters: **Access**, **Usage**, and **Quality**.

• **Access:** This parameter evaluates the availability of financial services, such as the number of bank branches, ATMs, and other financial outlets per population.

• **Usage:** This parameter measures how actively people use financial services, such as savings accounts, loans, or insurance policies.

• **Quality:** While not mentioned in the question, this parameter assesses the effectiveness and efficiency of financial services provided.

• The **FI-Index** is a comprehensive measure that ranges from **0 to 100**, where 0 represents complete financial exclusion and 100 signifies full financial inclusion.

• *Hence, both I (Access) and II (Usage) are correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Reserve Bank of India:**

• The **RBI** introduced the **FI-Index** to provide a comprehensive tool for policymakers and researchers to track financial inclusion progress.

• This index is released annually and incorporates data from **21 parameters**, grouped into the three mentioned dimensions.

• **Financial Inclusion:**

• Financial inclusion aims to provide affordable financial services to all individuals, especially marginalized and underserved communities.

• It includes services such as **banking, credit, insurance, and digital payments**.

• **Government Initiatives:**

• The Government of India has launched programs like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** to enhance financial inclusion.

• PMJDY focuses on providing universal access to banking facilities, financial literacy, and insurance coverage.

• **Global Context:**

• Similar indices exist globally, such as the **Global Findex Database** by the **World Bank**, which measures financial inclusion worldwide.

• India’s FI-Index aligns with international efforts to track progress toward achieving **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 8.10.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana:**

• Launched on **28th August 2014**, PMJDY aims to provide universal banking access.

• It has led to the opening of over **48 crore bank accounts** as of **2023**.

• **Digital Financial Services:**

• India’s financial inclusion efforts are bolstered by the rise of digital services like **UPI** and mobile banking.

• UPI (Unified Payments Interface) has revolutionized payment systems, processing over **10 billion transactions monthly** in **2023**.

questions.question: What is India's position in the World Press Freedom Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**151st**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **India ranked 151st** on the **World Press Freedom Index 2025**, reflecting a decline in press freedom within the country.

• The **World Press Freedom Index** is published annually by the **Reporters Without Borders (RSF)**, which evaluates the level of press freedom in 180 countries and territories.

• The ranking is based on indicators like **media independence, safety of journalists, legal framework, and the plurality of opinions**.

• India’s position has been affected by **increasing restrictions on journalists, censorship, and threats to media personnel**.

• The top-ranked countries on the index include **Norway, Denmark, and Sweden**, while countries like **North Korea and Eritrea** are ranked at the bottom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **World Press Freedom Index:**

• Introduced in **2002** by **Reporters Without Borders (RSF)**, the index evaluates the environment for journalism in 180 countries.

• The index uses five indicators: **political context, legal framework, economic factors, sociocultural context, and safety of journalists**.

• The aim of the index is to promote and safeguard **freedom of information** and press rights across the globe.

• **India's Declining Press Freedom:**

• India’s decline in rankings is attributed to **violence against journalists, internet blackouts, and governmental pressures**.

• Instances of **censorship and restrictions on critical reporting** have increased significantly in recent years.

• Journalists reporting on sensitive topics like **corruption, politics, or human rights** often face threats or legal actions.

• **Top-ranked Countries:**

• **Norway** has consistently ranked first in the index due to its strong commitment to press freedom.

• **Denmark and Sweden** also rank high, reflecting their democratic values and protection of press rights.

• **Bottom-ranked Countries:**

• **North Korea** and **Eritrea** are at the bottom of the index due to their **repressive regimes** and complete state control over media.

• Journalists in these countries face severe restrictions and risks, including imprisonment and violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Role of Reporters Without Borders (RSF):**

• RSF is an independent non-governmental organization that advocates for **media freedom and access to information**.

• It provides support to **journalists in danger** and promotes the universal right to freedom of expression.

• **Challenges to Press Freedom in India:**

• India faces challenges like **political interference in media, lack of safety for journalists, and increasing digital surveillance**.

• The rise of **fake news** and online trolling has also contributed to creating a hostile environment for journalists.

• **Global Trends:**

• Globally, press freedom is under threat with increasing instances of **censorship, disinformation, and attacks on media personnel**.

• Countries with strong press freedom often have **independent judiciary systems, transparent governance, and public trust**.

53

questions.question: The Export Preparedness Index in India is based on how many pillars?

• The **Export Preparedness Index (EPI)** in India is based on **four pillars**. These pillars provide a comprehensive framework for evaluating the export readiness of states and union territories. 
• The **four pillars** of the EPI include **Policy, Business Ecosystem, Export Ecosystem, and Export Performance**. 
• **Policy:** This pillar evaluates the regulatory framework, trade policies, and institutional support provided by states to promote exports. 
• **Business Ecosystem:** It assesses the ease of doing business, infrastructure development, and the overall environment for businesses to thrive. 
• **Export Ecosystem:** This evaluates factors like logistics, export infrastructure, and support mechanisms that facilitate exports. 
• **Export Performance:** This pillar measures the actual performance of states in terms of export volumes and growth trends. 
• The EPI was developed by the **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the Institute of Competiti

questions.question: The World Wetlands Day 2025 was celebrated at which of the following place of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gonda**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The World Wetlands Day** is observed annually on **February 2nd** to raise global awareness about the vital role of wetlands for people and the planet. 
• The theme for **World Wetlands Day 2025** emphasizes the importance of preserving and restoring wetlands, which are crucial for biodiversity, climate regulation, and water purification. 
• In Uttar Pradesh, the celebrations of World Wetlands Day 2025 were held in **Gonda**, showcasing efforts to conserve wetlands in the region, particularly focusing on the **Sarayu River and nearby wetlands.** 
• Uttar Pradesh is home to important wetlands like **Sandi Bird Sanctuary, Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary, and Sur Sarovar Bird Sanctuary**, which are significant for ecological balance and biodiversity conservation. 
• The event in Gonda aimed to involve local communities, students, and policymakers to discuss the importance of wetlands and promote sustainable practices to protect them. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Wetlands**: 
• Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, either permanently or seasonally, including marshes, swamps, bogs, and mangroves. 
• They act as **natural water filters**, store carbon, and provide critical habitats for a wide range of species. 
• Globally, wetlands cover about **6% of the Earth's surface**, but they are disappearing three times faster than forests. 
• **Ramsar Convention**: 
• The Ramsar Convention, signed in **1971** in Ramsar, Iran, is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. 
• India is a signatory to the convention, with **75 Ramsar sites** as of 2023, covering an area of over 13 lakh hectares. 
• **Sarayu River Wetlands**: 
• The wetlands along the **Sarayu River** are ecologically rich and provide livelihood support to local communities. 
• They are significant for migratory birds and aquatic biodiversity, making them an integral part of conservation discussions in Uttar Pradesh. 
• **Importance of Wetlands in India**: 
• India's wetlands are crucial for water security, flood control, and supporting agriculture and fisheries. 
• Initiatives like **National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA)** aim to protect and restore wetlands across the country. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **World Wetlands Day History**: 
• The day marks the date of the **adoption of the Ramsar Convention** on Wetlands on February 2, 1971. 
• It was first celebrated in **1997** to raise awareness about the importance of wetlands globally. 
• **Wetland Conservation Challenges**: 
• Urbanization, pollution, and agricultural expansion are major threats to wetlands in India. 
• Efforts like afforestation, reducing pollutant discharge, and community involvement are critical for wetland conservation. </ul

questions.question: The Bandipur Tiger Reserve is in _______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Bandipur Tiger Reserve** is located in the state of **Karnataka**, in southern India.
 
• It was established in **1974** as part of Project Tiger, a conservation program launched by the Government of India to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
• The reserve is part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**, which encompasses parts of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala, making it one of the largest protected areas in India.
 
• The Bandipur Tiger Reserve covers an area of approximately **874 square kilometers** and is known for its rich biodiversity, including Bengal tigers, Indian elephants, leopards, and various other species.
 
• It is famous for its dry deciduous forests, tropical mixed deciduous forests, and grassy woodlands, offering a diverse habitat for wildlife.

questions.question: The operation of a satellite launch vehicle is based on which of the following?

• **Newton's third law of motion** states that **for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction**. This principle is fundamental to the operation of a satellite launch vehicle.

• During the launch, the rocket engines expel gases at high speed in the downward direction (action), and as a result, the rocket is propelled upward (reaction).

• The expulsion of gases creates a force that pushes the rocket upward, overcoming gravity and atmospheric resistance. This is a direct application of Newton's third law.

• The launch vehicle achieves sufficient velocity to reach orbit by continuously applying this principle through the stages of the rocket.

questions.question: In 2024, which country became the first in the world to develop a wooden satellite named LignoSat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Japan** became the first country to develop a **wooden satellite** named **LignoSat** in **2024**. 
• The satellite was developed through a collaboration between **Kyoto University** and **Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd.**, a leading Japanese wood-processing company. 
• **LignoSat** is designed to explore the potential of using wood as a sustainable and environmentally friendly material for space exploration. 
• The satellite aims to address the issue of **space debris**, as wooden materials are expected to burn up completely upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere, leaving no harmful residue. 
• This innovation represents a significant step in the field of **green technology** and sustainable space science, contributing to global efforts to reduce space debris. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Wooden Satellite Technology:** 
• Wooden satellites like **LignoSat** are designed to use **treated wood** that can withstand the extreme conditions of space, including radiation, vacuum pressure, and temperature fluctuations. 
• The use of wood minimizes the environmental impact of satellite launches and de-orbiting, as it fully burns upon re-entry without creating additional space debris. 
• **Space Debris Issue:** 
• Space debris refers to defunct satellites, spent rocket stages, and fragments from collisions, which pose significant risks to operational satellites and spacecraft. 
• According to estimates, there are over **27,000 pieces of space debris** tracked by the U.S. Department of Defense. 
• Wooden satellites provide a potential solution by being biodegradable and reducing long-term space pollution. 
• **Japan's Leadership in Innovation:** 
• Japan is recognized globally for its advancements in **technology** and **environmental sustainability**. 
• Projects like **LignoSat** reflect Japan's commitment to innovation in **green technology** and eco-friendly scientific solutions. 
• **Other Countries' Initiatives in Space Technology:** 
• **Russia** and **China** have focused on traditional materials for satellites, prioritizing durability and cost-efficiency over environmental concerns. 
• **Israel** is known for its advancements in miniaturized satellite technology but has not ventured into wooden satellite development. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Wooden Satellite Development:** 
• The wood used in **LignoSat** is treated to resist **weathering and insect damage**, making it viable for space applications.

questions.question: In India, how many policy statements are mandated by the Fiscal responsibility and budget management act along with the budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act**, enacted in **2003**, aims to institutionalize financial discipline, reduce India’s fiscal deficit, and improve macroeconomic management.
 
• Under the FRBM Act, the government is required to present **three policy statements** to Parliament along with the Union Budget. These include:
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement:** This outlines the government’s fiscal strategy, including revenue generation and expenditure management.
 
• **Macroeconomic Framework Statement:** This provides an overview of the macroeconomic outlook for the country, including growth projections, inflation trends, and other key economic indicators.
 
• **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement:** This contains three-year rolling targets for fiscal indicators, such as revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and debt levels.
 
 
 
• The FRBM Act mandates transparency and accountability in fiscal operations and aims to create a framework for the government to manage its finances prudently.
 
• Regular monitoring and presentation of these statements provide a clear roadmap for fiscal management and help in achieving fiscal consolidation targets.
 
• **Hence, the correct answer is Three.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM):**

 
 
• The FRBM Act was enacted by the Government of India in **2003** to improve fiscal discipline and reduce the fiscal deficit.
 
• It sets targets for **revenue deficit** and **fiscal deficit** to ensure sustainable economic growth.
 
• The Act mandates the government to ensure transparency in fiscal operations and provide periodic updates through reports to Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement:**
 
 
• This statement is a part of the FRBM Act requirements and outlines the government’s fiscal policies, including expenditure priorities, revenue generation methods, and debt reduction strategies.
 
• It highlights the measures required to achieve short-term and long-term fiscal goals.
 
 
 
• **Macroeconomic Framework Statement:**
 
 
• This statement provides an overview of the economy’s performance and projections for key macroeconomic variables, such as **GDP growth, inflation rate, and fiscal deficit.**
 
• It helps policymakers and stakeholders understand the broader economic environment in which fiscal decisions are being made.
 
 
 
• **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement:**
 
 
• This statement provides rolling targets for three years for key fiscal indicators like **revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and debt levels.**
 
• It ensures that fiscal policy aligns with long-term sustainability goals.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• Despite being a landmark legislation, the FRBM Act has faced challenges due to global economic uncertainties, natural disasters, and changes in government priorities.
 
• Amendments to the Act have been made over the years to adapt to changing economic conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FRBM Act Amendment (2018):**

 
 
• The amendment introduced a new fiscal deficit target of **3% of GDP**, with a deviation of up to **0.5%** under special circumstances.
 
• It replaced the older metrics with the concept of **debt-to-GDP ratio** as a key fiscal indicator.
 
 
 
• **Role of Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG):**
 
 
• The CAG is tasked with monitoring the compliance of the government with the fiscal targets set under the FRBM Act.
 
• It provides independent audits and reports to ensure adherence to fiscal responsibility norms.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Many countries, including **New Zealand, Canada, and the UK**, have adopted fiscal responsibility legislation to ensure sound financial management and accountability.
 
• India’s FRBM Act aligns with global best practices while addressing local economic challenges.

questions.question: In which year was the Competition Act passed by the Parliament in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Competition Act** was passed by the **Parliament of India in 2002** and came into effect on **13 January 2003**.
 
• This act was enacted to replace the **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 (MRTP Act)**, which had become outdated in addressing the modern economic framework and competition issues.
 
• The **Competition Commission of India (CCI)** was established under this act to promote competition, prevent practices that have an adverse effect on competition, and protect the interests of consumers.
 
• The act focuses on **prohibition of anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulation of combinations (mergers and acquisitions)** that may harm competition.
 
• The **Competition Act, 2002**, aligns India’s economic regulations with the liberalized and globalized economic environment of the 21st century, promoting fair competition in the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of the Competition Act, 2002:**

 
 
• To prevent practices that have an **adverse effect on competition**.
 
• To promote and sustain **competition in markets**.
 
• To protect the **interests of consumers**.
 
• To ensure **freedom of trade** carried on by participants in markets in India.
 
 
 
• **Competition Commission of India (CCI):**
 
 
• The CCI is a **statutory body** established under the Competition Act, 2002.
 
• It is tasked with eliminating practices that affect competition and regulating mergers or acquisitions to ensure they do not harm market competition.
 
• The CCI comprises a **Chairperson and 6 members**, appointed by the Central Government.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Competition Act:**
 
 
• It **prohibits anti-competitive agreements**, such as cartels, that can harm competition.
 
• It addresses the **abuse of dominant position** by enterprises, ensuring that no entity exploits its market power unfairly.
 
• It regulates **mergers, acquisitions, and combinations** to prevent concentration of market power.
 
 
 
• **Replacement of MRTP Act:**
 
 
• The **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act** of 1969 aimed to curb monopolistic practices but was deemed inadequate for a liberalized economic environment.
 
• The Competition Act, 2002, was introduced to address modern economic challenges like globalization and ensure fair competition.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The act fosters a **healthy competitive environment**, ensuring efficiency and innovation in the market.
 
• It enhances **consumer welfare** by ensuring fair pricing and quality products.
 
• The act plays a pivotal role in preventing exploitation by monopolies or cartels.

questions.question: In which of the following valleys, over 97% of India's coal reserves are located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi and Godavari Valleys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India’s coal reserves:** Over **97% of India's coal reserves** are concentrated in the valleys of **Damodar, Sone, Mahanadi, and Godavari**, making them the most significant coal-bearing regions.
 
• **Damodar Valley:** Known as the **"Ruhr of India"**, it is one of the primary coal-producing regions, spanning states like **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**. Major coalfields include **Jharia, Bokaro, and Raniganj**.
 
• **Sone Valley:** Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, this valley hosts significant coal reserves, contributing to India’s energy sector.
 
• **Mahanadi Valley:** Found in **Odisha**, major coalfields like **Talcher** and **Ib Valley** are situated here. This region is a key supplier of thermal coal for power generation.
 
• **Godavari Valley:** Located in **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**, the **Singareni coalfields** are prominent here, known for producing high-grade coal.
 
• **Economic significance:** These valleys play a crucial role in India’s energy security, as coal is the primary source for electricity generation and industrial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Damodar Valley:**

 
 
• It is known for its historical coal mining activities dating back to colonial times.
 
• Major coalfields include **Jharia** (famous for its coking coal), **Bokaro**, and **Raniganj**.
 
• Coal from this region is extensively used in steel production and thermal power generation.
 
 
 
• **Sone Valley:**
 
 
• This valley is located primarily in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It contains coalfields like **Singrauli**, which supply coal for power plants such as NTPC Singrauli.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi Valley:**
 
 
• Located in **Odisha**, it includes major coalfields such as **Talcher** and **Ib Valley**.
 
• Coal from this region is used for thermal power generation and industrial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Godavari Valley:**
 
 
• This valley spans **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It is home to the **Singareni Collieries**, which produce high-quality coal.
 
• Coal from this region is used in power plants and other industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Coal:**
 
 
• Coal contributes to over **55%** of India’s electricity generation.
 
• India ranks as the **second-largest coal producer** globally, after China.
 
• Coal is vital for industries like steel, cement, and chemicals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coal Types in India:**

 
 
• **Anthracite:** Found in small quantities; used for heating purposes.
 
• **Bituminous:** Most abundant type; used in power generation and industries.
 
• **Lignite:** Found in Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan; used for electricity generation.
 
• **Peat:** Least carbon content; found in small quantities.
 
 
 
• **Coal Mining in India:**
 
 
• Managed primarily by **Coal India Limited (CIL)**, a government-owned entity.
 
• India’s coal production reached **893.08 million tonnes** in **2022-23**.
 
• Coal blocks are allocated to private players under **auction schemes**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Coal mining leads to deforestation, soil erosion, and air pollution.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote **clean coal technologies** and renewable energy sources to reduce dependency on coal.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana Yojana (RVY)?

I. It is a Central Sector Scheme.

II. It is a Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY)** is a **Central Sector Scheme** funded fully by the Government of India. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• The scheme is targeted at providing **physical aids and assisted-living devices to senior citizens belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category**. It aims to improve the quality of life for the elderly population.
 
• The funds for the scheme are drawn from the **Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund**, which was established under the 2015-16 Budget. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• Under the scheme, devices such as hearing aids, wheelchairs, walkers, spectacles, and other assistive devices are distributed to eligible senior citizens.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO)**, a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**

 
 
• Beneficiaries must belong to the **BPL category** and should be senior citizens aged 60 years or above.
 
• Preference is given to senior citizens suffering from age-related disabilities such as low vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, and locomotor disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme provides one-time free distribution of physical aids and assisted-living devices to eligible beneficiaries.
 
• Devices include **walking sticks, elbow crutches, walkers, tripods/quadrupods, hearing aids, spectacles, and dentures**.
 
• The devices aim to assist senior citizens in carrying out daily activities and improving their mobility and independence.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Process:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented in camps organized at district levels across India.
 
• Beneficiaries are identified through a process involving gram panchayats, municipal bodies, and urban local bodies.
 
 
 
• **Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund:**
 
 
• This fund was established as per the **Finance Act, 2015**, using unclaimed funds from schemes such as small savings and other similar programs.
 
• The fund is utilized for the welfare of senior citizens, including implementing schemes like RVY.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund:** It serves as a financial reservoir for schemes aimed at improving the lives of senior citizens in India. The fund ensures the sustained implementation of initiatives like RVY.
 
• **Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO):** ALIMCO is a key player in the implementation of RVY. It manufactures and supplies high-quality assistive devices to beneficiaries under the scheme.
 
• **Focus on Accessibility:** RVY emphasizes improving accessibility and mobility for senior citizens, thereby enabling them to lead a dignified life.
 
• **Inclusive Approach:** The scheme ensures that senior citizens from rural and urban areas, especially those from marginalized communities, are given due importance during beneficiary identification.

questions.question: During the Gupta period, 'Bhagvatism', which emphasized bhakti and ahimsa, centered on the worship of which deity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Bhagvatism** emerged during the **Gupta period**, emphasizing **bhakti** (devotion) and **ahimsa** (non-violence), which were central tenets of Hindu philosophy. 
• It was primarily centered on the worship of **Lord Vishnu**, who was considered the preserver in the Hindu trinity of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. 
• During the Gupta period, **Vaishnavism** (worship of Vishnu) gained prominence and became one of the dominant religious practices. 
• Bhagvatism promoted the idea of a personal relationship with God through devotion and love, marking a shift from ritualistic practices to emotional and spiritual connection. 
• The Gupta rulers, such as **Chandragupta II**, were great patrons of Vaishnavism, and many temples dedicated to Vishnu were built during this era. 
• Texts like the **Bhagavad Gita** and **Puranas**, especially the Vishnu Purana, played a significant role in spreading the teachings of Bhagvatism and strengthening its philosophical base. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Lord Vishnu:** 
• He is known as the **preserver** in the Hindu trinity and is associated with qualities such as compassion, protection, and sustenance. 
• Vishnu is often depicted as resting on the cosmic serpent **Shesha**, with his consort **Lakshmi**, the goddess of wealth, by his side. 
• His ten incarnations, known as the **Dashavatara**, include famous forms like **Rama**, **Krishna**, and **Narasimha**. 
• Vishnu Purana and Bhagavad Gita serve as key texts elaborating on his role and teachings, emphasizing dharma and devotion. 
• **The Gupta Empire:** 
• The Gupta period (320-550 CE) is known as the **Golden Age** of India for its advancements in art, literature, science, and religion. 
• The rulers were patrons of Hinduism, especially Vaishnavism, and contributed to temple architecture and iconography. 
• Key temples dedicated to Vishnu include the **Dashavatara Temple** at Deogarh and other structures showcasing intricate carvings and depictions of Vishnu’s avatars. 
• **Bhakti Movement:** 
• Bhagvatism laid the foundation for the later **Bhakti Movement**, which spread across India during medieval times. 
• It emphasized devotion over rituals, promoting a personal connection with God. 
• Saints like **Meerabai**, **Kabir**, and **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu** carried forward the ideals of bhakti, making religion accessible to all social classes. 
• **Other Deities in Hinduism:** 
• **Shiva:** Known as the destroyer, worshipped in Shaivism, he symbolizes transformation and renewal. 
• **Brahma:** The creator in the Hindu trinity, though his worship declined significantly over time. 
• **Indra:** A Vedic deity associated with rain and thunder, primarily worshipped during earlier Vedic times but less prominent during the Gupta era. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Bhagavad Gita:** 
• It is part of the **Mahabharata**, a sacred text advocating devotion, dharma, and selfless action. 
• The Gita serves as a philosophical guide for understanding the principles of Bhagvatism. 
• **Vaishnavism’s Influence:** 
• Many Gupta coins featured images of Vishnu and his avatars, showcasing the empire's allegiance to Vaishnavism. 
• The religious practices of the time were inclusive, with a focus on unity and spiritual growth. 
• **Ahimsa:** 
• This principle of non-violence was integral to Bhagvatism and influenced subsequent religious movements like Jainism and Buddhism.
